Case study · Product design

Be positive: making blood donation a habit.

A community app that reminds donors when they can give again, shows how much blood is in stock in each city and rewards regular donors with real perks.

ProjectBe positive · DECODE
RoleProduct design
TimelineIdea born in 2020 · I joined in 2025
Team2 full stack engineers, PM, QA and me
ScopeMarket research · Analysis · Feature prioritisation · Personas and journey · User flows · App architecture · UI and branding

The challenge

Make people give blood more often and more regularly.

Forgetting

Donors often forget when they are eligible to give again after their last donation.

Where to go

There was no complete list of possible donation spots.

How much is needed

People wanted to know how much blood is in stock in each city.

The benefits

The benefits of donating blood in Croatia were hard to find out.

Where it started

The idea began at a company hackathon in 2020, when a team of DECODErs wanted to build something that would outlive the hackathon. The first version showed live blood supply levels in transfusion centers, using data from the Croatian Institute for Transfusion Medicine and its subsidiaries, and notified donors when stock for their blood type ran low.

I joined the team in 2025 to take the idea to the next level with the features users said they needed.

The idea for the app came from an issue we all experience as donors – forgetting about it. And since it is such an important and noble act, we didn’t want to forget it ever again.

Ivan Trogrlić, Team Lead at DECODE

Research

What I did

  • Interviewed blood donors
  • Read Google reviews of the previous app
  • Studied similar apps around the world, with their features and bottlenecks
  • Drew up personas and their journey

What it led to

  • A clear list of what donors actually need
  • User flows and an app architecture built around those needs
  • A focus on reminders, tracking and rewards

Key decisions

Gamified donating

Regular donations unlock real perks, including free healthcare in Croatia and free public transit in Zagreb.

Easy tracking

Donors can follow their own donations and see when they can give again.

Visual identity

The logo joins the letter B with a red cross, with negative space that forms a heart. It stands for care, compassion and life-saving donations. The deep red signals blood, health and urgency, and the white space adds clarity and trust.

Poppins

A geometric sans-serif with uniform strokes and rounded letterforms. Clean, modern and friendly, and easy to read in digital interfaces.

Screens

What we expect these screens to achieve

More timely donations

Seeing which blood types are running low helps donors give when it matters most.

A habit that sticks

A visible donation count and progress toward perks make regular giving rewarding.

Fewer forgotten donations

A clear countdown to the next eligible date keeps donors on track.

Effortless tracking

Logging a donation takes a few taps, so the record stays complete.

Reminders you can trust

An accurate history means accurate eligibility dates and timely reminders.

Motivation to continue

A success message and a growing count celebrate every donation.

Find where to donate.

Donation spots are shown on a map, so donors can see the nearest center and open it for details.

Where it stands

The first version is live on the App Store and Google Play with three cities and their clinical centers, and more are coming as data becomes available.

The new version, with the gamification and donation tracking, is coming soon to both stores.
